newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU posts 5.3 bln Ecu trade deficit with CIS in 1995.
newsitem.headline: EU posts 5.3 bln Ecu trade deficit with CIS in 1995.

text.p: The European Union posted a 5.3 billion European currency units ($6.63 billion) trade deficit in 1995 with states making up the former Soviet Union.

Figures released on Thursday by Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, show the EU imports from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) were worth 23.2 billion Ecus in 1995 -- an 8.8 percent increase on the previous year.
EU exports to the CIS rose 11.5 percent to 17.9 billion Ecus.
Although both EU imports and exports rose, the trade deficit remained roughly the same, Eurostat said.
The figures only include trade with 12 EU states. Figures for Finland, Austria and Sweden -- which joined the union last year -- have not been included.
Petroleum and related products were the biggest EU import, accounting for 27 percent of trade and worth 6.2 billion Ecus.
Nearly a quarter of all EU exports to the CIS were taken up by manufactured products -- particularly industrial machinery. ($1 = 0.80 Ecu)
